Subject: Polaris integration: auth & key management next steps

Hi Elena / Polaris security team —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the auth path for the integration:

What we learned
- You want an inference endpoint behind strict access controls, predictable rotation, and auditability for regulator requests.
- Two candidate approaches on the table: long-lived API keys scoped per-team vs service-account-based short-lived tokens integrated with your IdP.
- Priority: secure key rotation + ability to audit per-request identity (who, which environment).

Redwood recommendation (high level)
- Use service accounts + short-lived JWTs issued by Polaris IdP (OIDC) and exchanged for Redwood ephemeral tokens (30m default).
- Support an alternate path for partner tooling that uses scoped API keys with enforced rotation and usage limits (for CI/CD and legacy apps).
- Enable region-based routing so dev traffic in us-west stays local, with automatic fallback to hosted variants if capacity constraints occur.

Concrete next steps
1) Polaris security to confirm IdP/OIDC metadata and test client credentials.
2) We’ll send a short integration checklist and a proposed auth flow diagram (attached).
3) Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive to validate token exchange and sample SDK usage — days/times that work?

Attachments: integration-checklist.pdf (minimal checklist), redwood-auth-proposal.pdf (flow diagram + rotation cadence).

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Elena — Naomi flagged this to me; looped in specifics below and a short checklist for the Thursday deep-dive. I'm Redwood's solutions engineer on this account.

Short answers to your questions
- Redwood accepts IdP-signed JWTs and performs an OAuth2 token-exchange on our side. This means Polaris can mint short-lived, signed assertions (recommended 5-15m TTL) and Redwood will exchange for an ephemeral inference token bound to the service account.
- API-key scoping: we support per-route and per-model scoping, plus metadata tags (team, environment). Keys can be constrained by quota and allowed IP ranges.

Recommended auth architecture (both secure and practical)
1) Create dedicated service accounts per-environment (prod/stage/dev) in Polaris IdP.
2) Polaris mints a signed JWT using a service private key.
3) Redwood's token-exchange endpoint verifies the JWT (kid lookup via Polaris JWKS), issues an ephemeral token for the requested scope (default 30m), and logs the exchange event for audit.
4) SDKs (we'll provide Node/Python/Go snippets) automatically refresh tokens and cache them in memory; token refresh uses the exchange endpoint and rotates transparently.
5) For CI/CD or automated agents that cannot do OIDC, use scoped API keys with an enforced 90-day rotation policy and automated rotation alerts.

Key rotation & audit
- Rotation: private keys at Polaris: rotate on a 90-day cadence; ephemeral tokens <1h.
- Audit: every token exchange emits a structured audit event (timestamp, service_account, requested_scope, ip, user_agent). We can stream these to your SIEM or S3 bucket.

Routing and fallbacks (short note)
- Region-based routing: client SDKs attach region hint; our routing policy sends requests to closest cluster.
- Fallback: if dedicated private pool is saturated, requests can degrade to hosted pool with a header that indicates fallback so you can correlate cost/latency.

Thursday deep-dive checklist (proposed agenda)
- Exchange OIDC metadata & test creds (10m)
- Walk token exchange flow with sample request/response (20m)
- SDK demo: ephemeral token refresh + structured output example (15m)
- Requirements: embeddings/reranker access patterns and any per-request PII routing (15m)

Attaching: redwood-auth-proposal.pdf with a diagram and example audit event JSON. Looking forward to the call — if Thursday 10:00 PST works, I'll send a calendar invite and draft an agenda.
